part.text:
[
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Use `high` for meaningful implementation, research, review, and synthesis. / Use `xhigh` for hard planning, debugging, synthesis, and adversarial review.",
    "scenario": "The orchestrator assigns a synthesis lane that merges three research reports into one design document.",
    "policy_answer": "Both `high` and `xhigh` are named as the correct effort for synthesis.",
    "fix": "Assign synthesis to one tier, for example `high` for routine synthesis and `xhigh` only for adversarial or multi-source synthesis."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Use `xhigh` for hard planning, debugging, synthesis, and adversarial review. / | Difficult implementation, refactoring, debugging, or test construction | Claude with Opus 5.5 | Sonnet 5.5 at `xhigh`; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol at `xhigh` | / | Claude | Opus 5.5 at `high` |",
    "scenario": "The orchestrator routes a debugging lane for a failing production migration.",
    "policy_answer": "The fleet table sends debugging to Opus 5.5 with no effort, so the default `high` applies. The effort rules say debugging uses `xhigh`.",
    "fix": "State the effort in each lane row, or say which source wins when the effort list and the fleet default disagree."
  },
  {
    "type": "ambiguity",
    "quote": "When the caller pins only the worker CLI, use that CLI's default route or a more specific fleet route on it. Mark the lane `Unrouted` when none fits. / Do not use it as a coding fallback.",
    "scenario": "The caller pins the Grok CLI and asks for a multi-file implementation lane.",
    "policy_answer": "The pinned-CLI rule routes the lane to Grok 4.7 at `high`. The Grok row and its `Keep for` column exclude coding. The text does not say if this lane is routed or `Unrouted`.",
    "fix": "State that a pinned CLI whose default route hits a keep-away clue for the lane makes the lane `Unrouted`."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Treat their findings as leads, not verdicts. / Review Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, or Fable 5.1 work with GPT-6.1 Sol, Astra, or Grok 4.7.",
    "scenario": "Grok 4.7 reviews an Opus 5.5 implementation and reports a defect.",
    "policy_answer": "The leads section lists Grok 4.7 as a weaker model whose findings need reproduction. The pairing section lists Grok 4.7 as a capable reviewer whose verdict can stand.",
    "fix": "State whether a Grok 4.7 reviewer verdict needs reproduction, and remove Grok 4.7 from one of the two lists."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Keep other models at `medium` or above. / GPT-6.1 Sol at `low` or `medium`; GLM-5.3 Flash / Opus 5.5 at `low`",
    "scenario": "The orchestrator picks the `low` fallback for a high-volume extraction lane, or the `low` Opus fallback in the budget row.",
    "policy_answer": "The lane table lists `low` values. The effort section bans values under `medium` for `other models`, and `other` is not defined.",
    "fix": "Define `other models` or delete the sentence, and keep only the per-model floors from the fleet table."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Use `max` when the caller requires one worker or a fixed delegation structure. / Use `max` for the hardest quality-first work with a clear stopping condition.",
    "scenario": "The caller requires one worker for a trivial rename sweep.",
    "policy_answer": "One rule forces `max`. The other rule reserves `max` for the hardest work. The lane gets `max` effort it does not need.",
    "fix": "Replace the rule with: when the caller requires one worker, do not use `ultra`, and keep the lane-appropriate effort."
  },
  {
    "type": "ambiguity",
    "quote": "| Edge-case discovery and confirmation across model families | OpenCode with GLM-5.3, Muse Spark 1.3, or Kimi K3 | Grok 4.7; GLM-5.3 Flash |",
    "scenario": "The orchestrator opens an edge-case lane and all three first-route models are available.",
    "policy_answer": "None. The row gives three models with no selection order. The fallback rule only covers unavailable routes. The parallel-run rule applies only `when the lane needs diverse edge cases`.",
    "fix": "Give a selection order among the three models, or state when one run versus parallel runs applies."
  },
  {
    "type": "gap",
    "quote": "Treat migrations and multi-file features as difficult implementation. Use the budget row only when the caller states a cost limit.",
    "scenario": "The caller states a hard cost limit and asks for a multi-file migration.",
    "policy_answer": "None. The budget row covers only `bounded coding or repository sweeps`. The difficult-implementation row has no cost-limited route. The cost limit has no effect.",
    "fix": "Add a cost-limited route for difficult implementation, for example Sonnet 5.5 at `high` with a stop budget."
  },
  {
    "type": "gap",
    "quote": "Kimi K3 when the harness preserves full history / Before launch, confirm only the selected configured identifier and effort control through host status or a targeted CLI check.",
    "scenario": "A long-context lane falls back to Kimi K3, and the orchestrator must verify the route before launch.",
    "policy_answer": "The fallback requires a harness that preserves full history. The verification step checks only the identifier and the effort. No check for history preservation exists.",
    "fix": "Add a verification step for harness history preservation, or require caller confirmation before any Kimi K3 route."
  },
  {
    "type": "unsafe",
    "quote": "Cyber safeguards send most security work to Opus 4.8, which is outside this fleet. / Use only the fixed fleet.",
    "scenario": "A defensive security review on Opus 5.5 is rerouted by safeguards to Opus 4.8, and the worker returns a result.",
    "policy_answer": "None. The policy does not say if the safeguard-rerouted result counts as valid, as a failed identifier, or as an `Unrouted` lane.",
    "fix": "State that a safeguard reroute to a model outside the fleet counts as an unavailable route and triggers the listed fallback."
  }
]
